title: ooRexx owns every decision; the page only displays
summary: src/OodDesigner.cls owns the design: the model, the control catalogue (::RESOURCE oodKinds, one kind line per control, one action line per code-insertion action), the generator and the reader. site/designer.js displays the design and reports what the user did (a drop, a move, a property typed, a line of code) as a message to an OodDesign object in an ooRexx/WASM session. The object refuses what would break the program and says why (a control named execute, a style the control does not take, an event it does not have, a line starting ::, a bad binding). src/OodGraph.cls owns graph edits; src/OodUi.cls holds every text the designer shows (strings.en, strings.de) read by OodNls. JavaScript is used for pointer and drag events, and for T(key) because a page text is needed at once.
invariants: Never decide a design rule in JavaScript: add it to OodDesign and let the page show the refusal.
A refusal is raise syntax 93.900 array(oodT(key, ...)): a translated message, keyed in OodUi en and de; tests/t04_ui.rex checks de has every en key with the same %n.
The code is the truth: a graph edit answers new code that goes through setEventCode/setMethod like typing.
A new control kind is one catalogue line; props= lists the properties it takes, and setProp refuses others.
